info.description:
Software verification API for Radius.

**Envelope.** JSON payloads are wrapped as `{success, data, error, meta}`. Failures use
the shared `ErrorEnvelope`; branch on `error.code`.

**Authentication.** Send `X-Radius-Organization-Id` and `X-Radius-API-Key` on every
non-health route. Both are declared as security schemes, not repeated as parameters.

**Stability.** Every tag and operation carries `x-stability` (`stable`, `beta`, `alpha`
or `internal`). The policy lives in `docs/api/STABILITY.md`. Clients must ignore unknown
response fields.

**Pagination.** List endpoints return the full array, except intent snapshot history
which takes `limit` and `cursor`. Cursors are opaque.

**Concurrency.** Intent reads return an `ETag`; intent writes accept `If-Match` and
answer 409 `INTENT_STALE` on a mismatch. `Idempotency-Key` makes creates replay-safe.

**Rate limits.** 429 carries `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-*` headers.

**Deprecation.** Deprecated operations are flagged `deprecated: true` and answer with
`Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers.

post.description:
Ingest one CI test report and re-score the analysis.

Evidence binding (any violation leaves the verdict untouched):

* ``commit_sha`` is required (422) and must equal the analysed head (409).
* The analysis must be completed (pending/running/failed/cancelled → 409)
  and must be the latest analysis
  of its pull request; results for a superseded head are stale (409).
* A malformed or empty report is rejected (422) before anything is stored.

Uploads accumulate: every distinct report for the analysis is kept, a
failure in any upload is sticky, executed cases are unioned when matching
selected tests, and replaying an identical body is idempotent. Selected
test files absent from (or only skipped in) the results keep the verdict at
``insufficient_evidence``.

post.description:
Connect a repository by ``owner/name`` through the GitHub App (no webhook).

The API asks GitHub which App installation covers the repository, reads the
repository metadata (id, default branch, clone URL, visibility) and stores
the installation id on the organization, which is all the worker needs to
clone, analyze and publish. Safe to repeat: an already connected repository
is returned (and reconnected if it had been disconnected).

post.description:
Analyze one pull request by number: fetch it from GitHub, queue an analysis.

This is the pull-based replacement for the ``pull_request`` webhook. The head
commit is read from GitHub, so the caller does not need a commit SHA. A
pending or running analysis of the same head commit is reused.

Pull open pull requests from GitHub (no webhook) and analyze them.

Draft pull requests are stored but not analyzed, and a head commit that already
has a live or finished analysis is not analyzed again (repeat syncs are cheap);
use the per-PR ``analyze`` route to analyze one explicitly. Without GitHub App credentials the stored
pull requests are returned unchanged (``meta.github = not_configured``).
GitHub failures are returned as errors, not swallowed.
Handle signed GitHub webhook deliveries.
